title: Renovations That Can Lower Commercial Property Insurance
metaTitle: Renovations That Can Lower Commercial Property Insurance
metaDescription: Water damage is a major driver of commercial property claims. These renovations cut water and fire risk and make your Winnipeg building a better risk.
excerpt: Water damage is a major driver of commercial property claims. These renovations cut water and fire risk and make your Winnipeg building a better risk.
answer: Renovations that reduce water, fire and theft risk can make your building easier to insure and sometimes lower your premium. Repair masonry, replace failing windows and supply lines, add leak protection, and update fire separations. Keep records for your broker, tell your insurer before work starts, and ask which upgrades earn credit with your carrier.

Infoassurance: 8 factors that influence the premium

blocks.x: Water damage is one of the biggest drivers of commercial property claims in Canada. A Gallagher Canada claims executive quoted by [Canadian Underwriter](https://canadianunderwriter.ca/news/claims/why-water-damage-claims-cost-the-industry-more-each-year-than-severe-weather-claims) in 2020 said half of the firm's commercial property claims were water-based. Some renovations can reduce that risk, which can sometimes help lower commercial property insurance costs.
You can't control the insurance market, but you can control how your building looks to an underwriter. Here's which upgrades reduce risk, and what to tell your insurer before work starts.
What insurers look at
**Age and condition of the roof and building envelope**
**Electrical, plumbing and heating systems:** age and type
**Fire protection:** sprinklers, alarms, monitoring, fire separations
**Water damage risk:** old supply lines, water heaters, basements
**Exterior condition:** masonry, windows, doors
**Occupancy:** restaurants and some uses carry higher risk
**Claims history**

Each insurer weighs these differently. [Infoassurance](https://infoassurance.ca/en/business-insurance/insurance/factors-influence-premium.aspx), a Quebec site from the Insurance Bureau of Canada and the Groupement des assureurs automobiles, lists building age, construction material, heating, sprinklers, type of business and claims history among the factors behind a business premium, so ask your broker how your insurer rates them.
Renovations that reduce risk

head: Upgrade
Risk it reduces
rows: Water entry, freeze-thaw damage, falling material
Plumbing supply line and water heater replacement
Leak sensors and automatic shutoff valves
Basement flooding during heavy rain or spring melt
Better exterior lighting and secure entries

blocks.x: In Winnipeg, plumbing, mechanical and electrical work needs a City-licensed contractor to apply for the permit, so check who is applying before work starts.
Keep good records
Underwriters can only rate what they know about. After any commercial renovation, give your broker:
The year and scope of each upgrade, with invoices and permits
Photos of the work
Updated system ages (roof, heating, plumbing, electrical)
An outdated system age in your insurer's file means your upgrades may not be counted.
Tell your insurer before you renovate
This step is easy to miss. Before construction starts:
**Notify your insurer** of the scope and schedule. Some policies require it.
**Ask about coverage during construction.** Larger projects may need builder's risk or course-of-construction coverage.
**Check vacancy clauses.** If the building or units will be empty during work, coverage may be limited after a certain number of days.

**Check your contractor's coverage.** Ask for a certificate of liability insurance and pull a [WCB Manitoba clearance letter](/blog/how-to-check-a-contractors-wcb-clearance-manitoba) before work begins.
Talk to your broker about credits

We found no published figure for how much any of these upgrades lowers a premium, so treat a saving as something to confirm, not a promise. Ask which specific improvements earn a credit or better terms with your carrier, and get it in writing. Start renewal conversations well before your renewal date so recent upgrades are counted.
The bottom line
The right commercial renovation can make your building safer, drier and easier to insure. Document the work and talk to your insurer before and after.
